subject: Deducer talking and listening to ImageJ (or any other Java app)

messages.author: 225c7cfd9a9e1c9d
messages.subject: Deducer talking and listening to ImageJ (or any other Java app)
parts:
Hi,
I'm a R developer working with an ImageJ plugin developer. We would like to make Deducer and ImageJ share the same R session, so that both of the two apps can updates variables and communicate via this R session. For example, selecting an item in the ImageJ plugin GUI would change a "data" var in R and Deducer would update the graph or the highlight part of the graph.
What would be the best way to do it?
I've tried to call a Session from JGR but failed, I've tried Rcaller and it works, so then I can call Deducer from RCaller but it looks strange to do so, doesn't it?
All our data is stored in a MongoDB database, but building a database listener is strange too, so...
Any advice would be great, thanks.

Deducer kicks ass!

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Deducer talking and listening to ImageJ (or any other Java app)
parts:
There are two ways that you can set up communication with R:

The first is to have a stand alone Java app (i.e. ImageJ), and use
RServe to start-up and communicate with an instance of R.

The second is to have the user start you app from within an R session.
This is the Deducer way of doing things. Here you would just put the
ImageJ jar into an R package. When the user loads the package, ImageJ
will be available.

Last summer one of the Google Summer of Code projects looked at
creating a bridge between R and ImageJ. The code was never released to
CRAN, but I've attached the package here as it might be useful for
your project.


Best,
Ian

On 03/08/2012 21:29, Ian Fellows wrote:
> There are two ways that you can set up communication with R:
>
> The first is to have a stand alone Java app (i.e. ImageJ), and use
> RServe to start-up and communicate with an instance of R.
Ok, so both ImageJ and Deducer would be able to get infos from R.

>
> The second is to have the user start you app from within an R session.
> This is the Deducer way of doing things. Here you would just put the
> ImageJ jar into an R package. When the user loads the package, ImageJ
> will be available.

Once it is launched, how can Deducer communicate, retrieve data from R
or send parameters to R? Are there listeners? Our only goal is to allow
request and response to R from Deducer and from ImageJ. So that if
ImageJ has to communicate with Deducer, it will send data to R before or
get data Deducer would have sent to R.

> CRAN, but I've attached the package here as it might be useful for
> your project.

look, thanks a lot for this outstanding reply!

This would not work with JGR/Deducer as they take the second approach.

>> This is the Deducer way of doing things. Here you would just put the
>> ImageJ jar into an R package. When the user loads the package, ImageJ

>

http://www.deducer.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php?n=Main.Development covers
some of this. Java classes can be called from R, and R
expressions/objects can be executed and manipulated in Java with
REngine (see: Deducer.eval). Take a look at some of the Deducer
plug-ins to see how this communication is managed. in particular
DeducerSpatial.

ian
